incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency spike detected in eu-west-1. SLO breach (p99 > 10s). Paging oncall.
Mia S.: Oncall Mia here, looking now. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-latency (eu-west-1). Starting triage.
Mia S.: Symptoms: SSE connections show long stalls (no chunks) then big catch-up. p95 ~350ms, p99 ~12.4s. Affected routes: /v1/stream (chat), /v1/events (streaming embeddings).
Raj P.: Any recent deploys or infra changes?
Mia S.: Deploy-bot shows no model/service deploys in the last 3h. There was an autoscale event ~20:40 UTC but nothing obvious.
Lucy: Can confirm proxies showing large write queues. Running quick probe: `curl -i https://edge.eu-west-1.redwood/health` and netstat on edge-proxy -> many ESTABLISHED with tx-queue growing.
Harold: Log tail from edge-proxy (paste):
```
2026-03-17T20:59:12Z edge-proxy x: proxy_write_timeout triggered for conn_id=98765
2026-03-17T20:59:13Z edge-proxy x: slow_consumer_evicted user=acct_42
2026-03-17T20:59:14Z edge-proxy x: write_backpressure high: 0.82
```
Mia S.: Mitigation plan: 1) scale streaming workers +2 2) enable slow-client eviction 3) decrease client window / max_inflight_chunks 4) route impacted enterprise accounts to polling fallback. I'll start with scaling.
SRE-Jackson: Running scale now:
```
kubectl scale deploy streaming-pool -n prod --replicas=6
```
Lucy: Pushing eviction config to edge-proxy (client_window 16 -> 8) as a canary.
incident-bot: Autoscaler: +2 streaming workers came online (new replicas healthy).
Mia S.: Partial improvement observed. p99 dropped from 12.4s -> 2.1s. Still above SLO and some clients are reconnecting due to eviction.
Customer Success: CS has flagged enterprise customers reporting 'long stalls then reconnect'—we're drafting customer comms and support playbook.
Raj P.: If eviction causes customer-visible reconnects, can we toggle streaming-fallback for affected accounts? Feature flag `streaming-fallback` exists.
Lucy: Toggling fallback for top-3 impacted accounts now (acct_42, acct_99, acct_18).
Mia S.: Fallback toggled for those accounts. Observed fewer reconnects, p99 now ~1.5s. Good short-term stability.
Harold: Hypothesis: bursty slow consumers (clients that read slowly) are causing proxy write buffers to pile up and slowing other streams (head-of-line). Collecting tcpdump + proxy histograms to S3: s3://incidents/6212349998/
SRE-Jackson: Added incident ticket + runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-backpressure
Mia S.: Short-term config change request: reduce proxy `max_inflight_chunks` 64 -> 32 and enable per-connection write buffer cap. Will stage as canary.
Raj P.: I'll stage the configmap update on canary edge-proxies (10%) then roll to full if metrics look good.
incident-bot: STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. No active paging. Manual closure required.
Mia S.: Handoff to Raj for the midnight shift. Notes: mitigated by scaling + eviction + account fallback. Customer impact: reconnects for a subset of accounts but no data loss. Artifacts: tcpdumps, proxy histograms, grafana panels saved in S3.
Mia S.: Follow-ups: reproduce with a synthetic slow-consumer load test, review batching and proxy async writes, evaluate whether to split streaming traffic by consumer class. Postmortem owner: Raj.
Raj P.: Taking handoff. I'll own the postmortem, coordinate with CS for external updates, and schedule a follow-up runbook update. Will post a draft in ~2h. :thumbsup:
